newsitem.title: USA: Streisand company to make TV movie on McCarthy.
newsitem.headline: Streisand company to make TV movie on McCarthy.

text.p: The life story of Representative Carolyn McCarthy, a nurse who entered politics after a gunman killed her husband in the Long Island Railroad massacre, will be depicted in a TV movie, her office announced Wednesday.

McCarthy, a life-long Republican in her Nassau County, Long Island district until she became a gun control advocate and ran successfully as a Democrat in last year's election, had previously declined dozens of movie offers.

She said in a statement that she agreed to Columbia TriStar Television developing a two-hour movie called "The Carolyn McCarthy Story" for NBC network in the 1997-98 season partly because of the involvement of Hollywood star Barbra Streisand's company, Barwood Productions.

"It would have been made with or without my agreement, and with my participation I can make sure that the incident is dealt with in a sensitive manner that isn't unecessarily painful to the families of victims," McCarthy said in a statement.

McCarthy's life was transformed Dec. 7, 1993, when gunman Colin Ferguson opened fire on a Long Island Rail Road commuter train, killing six people and wounding 19 others. McCarthy's husband of 30 years, stockbroker Dennis McCarthy, was killed and her son Kevin was shot in the head and hand and is still partially paralysed.

"People making this film see this as an inspirational story that can give hope to other people, people with learning disabilities or people working to overcome tragedies," she said referring to the recovery of her son, who has returned to work and study.
She said any money from the film would be put into the trust fund set up for her son "to make his future more secure".
McCarthy decided to run against incumbent Republican Dan Frisa when he voted to repeal the ban on assault weapons, and defeated him handily in last November's congressional race.
In a statement issued through NBC, Streisand said, "We are extremely proud that Carolyn McCarthy is allowing us to bring her remarkable story to television audiences."
No further details about the production of the movie were available.
